SeaStar Medical Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and
Provides Business Updates

 

Continued adoption of the QUELIMMUNE® therapy yielded 247% increase in net revenue compared to the third quarter of 2025

 

Achieved nearly 75% enrollment in the NEUTRALIZE-AKI pivotal clinical trial in adult patients with acute kidney injury (AKI) receiving CRRT

 

Reported statistically significant higher survival for QUELIMMUNE-treated patients versus comparator cohort at ASN Kidney Week 2026 late-breaking presentation

 

Fulfilled FDA post-approval requirements for SAVE Registry study

 

Webcast today at 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time

 

DENVER, CO (November 11, 2026) – SeaStar Medical Holding Corporation (Nasdaq: ICU), a commercial-stage healthcare company focused on transformational treatments for critically ill patients facing organ failure and potential loss of life, announced today financial results for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and provided business updates on key initiatives. 

 

“The strength of the QUELIMMUNE therapy adoption in this ultra-rare pediatric AKI market provides great promise for our pipeline indications,” said Eric Schlorff, CEO of SeaStar Medical. “And we continue to build momentum in educating the critical care pediatric health care community. In addition to several medical meeting presentations by Dr. Kevin Chung, our CMO, we have already begun sharing with critical care professionals the statistically significant higher survival in QUELIMMUNE-treated patients that was presented at the late-breaking presentation at ASN Kidney Week 2026.” 

 

Mr. Schlorff continued, “The NEUTRALIZE-AKI pivotal clinical trial has enrolled nearly 75% of its intended 339 patients, and we have already submitted the first module of the premarket approval application to the FDA in hopes that our modular submission will speed this potential approval.  Our Breakthrough Device Designation for this indication will also enable a priority review once we submit the final module with the NEUTRALIZE-AKI pivotal trial results, provided a positive outcome in the trial.”

 

Key Business Highlights

 

Since the beginning of the third quarter, SeaStar Medical’s key business updates include the following:

 

 

●

Expanded the use of the QUELIMMUNE (SCD-PED) therapy as a treatment for ultra-rare sepsis-associated AKI in pediatric patients receiving renal replacement therapy (RRT), increasing net revenue 247% to $635 thousand compared to the third quarter of 2025. Gross profit margins remained at greater than 90%.  

 

1
 

 

 

●

Presented at ASN Kidney Week 2026 real-world pediatric patient survival data from the commercial use of the QUELIMMUNE therapy based on results from the SAVE Registry of 50 critically ill pediatric patients with life-threatening sepsis-associated AKI. The QUELIMMUNE (SCD-PED) therapy group showed statistically significant higher survival in the primary analysis at Day 60, Day 90, and at hospital discharge versus comparator cohorts. No device-related adverse events occurred in patients treated with the QUELIMMUNE (SCD-PED) therapy.

 

 

●

Fulfilled FDA post-approval requirements for the SAVE Registry study for QUELIMMUNE for the treatment of sepsis-associated AKI in pediatric patients. FDA’s decision now enables hospitals to employ the QUELIMMUNE therapy without the research infrastructure that the SAVE Registry demanded, which may increase availability for these critically ill pediatric patients.

 

 

●

Advanced enrollment in the NEUTRALIZE-AKI pivotal clinical trial evaluating the SCD therapy as a potential treatment for adult patients with AKI in the ICU receiving continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). The trial is nearly 75% enrolled, with 251 of 339 patients enrolled to date. The NEUTRALIZE-AKI pivotal clinical trial is expected to complete enrollment by mid-year 2027.

 

 

●

Completed and submitted to the FDA the first module of a modular premarket approval (PMA) application for the potential approval of the SCD therapy as a treatment for adult patients with AKI in the ICU receiving CRRT.

 

 

●

Granted Breakthrough Device Designation from the FDA for the SCD therapy for the treatment of hyperinflammation in adult patients with sepsis or a septic condition. The Breakthrough Device Designation is a regulatory pathway designed to provide for accelerated development, assessment, and review for FDA approval of medical devices and potentially more effective treatments of life-threatening or irreversibly debilitating diseases or conditions. This marks the seventh Breakthrough Device Designation for the SCD therapy thus far across a range of indications.

 

 

●

Received dedicated International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Procedure Coding System (ICD-10-PCS codes) from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). These codes, which took effect on October 1, 2026, enable administrative, billing, and statistical reporting for the use of SeaStar Medical’s SCD therapy in patients with AKI requiring RRT in the inpatient hospital setting.

Financial Results for the Third Quarter 2026

 

Net revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, was approximately $0.6 million and $0.2 million, respectively, reflecting increased sales of QUELIMMUNE. 

 

Cost of goods sold for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, was $48 thousand and $14 thousand respectively.

 

Research and development expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, were $3.6 million and $1.9 million, respectively. The increase in research and development expenses was primarily driven by increased clinical research activities for the NEUTRALIZE-AKI pivotal clinical trial, SCD development costs, personnel, and payroll costs.

 

General and administrative expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, were approximately $1.6 million and $1.9 million, respectively. The decrease in general and administrative expenses was the result of a decline in personnel, legal, audit, and SEC-related costs, partially offset by increased professional services, director fees, and franchise taxes.

Other income (net) for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was approximately $0.1 million compared to other expense of approximately $0.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

 

Net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was approximately $4.5 million, or $1.03 per share on approximately 4.4 million weighted-average shares outstanding. This compares with a net loss of approximately $3.5 million, or $1.30 per share, on approximately 2.7 million weighted-average shares outstanding for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

 

Cash at September 30, 2026, was $4.0 million, which does not include the $3.3 million of gross proceeds from warrant exercises that occurred in October 2026. This compares to cash of $12.0 million at December 31, 2025.

About QUELIMMUNE

 

The QUELIMMUNE® (SCD-PED) therapy is being commercialized for children with AKI and sepsis or a septic condition weighing 10 kilograms or more and aged ≤22 years who are on antibiotics and being treated in the ICU with RRT. It was approved in February 2024 under a Humanitarian Device Exemption application.

 

Data from two clinical trials of the QUELIMMUNE therapy, published in Kidney Medicine, showed a 77% survival rate in patient treated with QUELIMMUNE versus standard of care, representing an approximate 50% reduction in loss of life compared to historical data in this patient population. No dialysis was required for survivors, and 87.5% of survivors had normal kidney function at Day 60 after ICU discharge.

 

The patented technology behind QUELIMMUNE is known as the Selective Cytopheretic Device (SCD) therapy and could have broad applications for treating the destructive hyperinflammation that shuts down organ function and causes loss of life. 

 

QUELIMMUNE was approved by FDA under a Humanitarian Device Exemption based on safety and probable benefit.  The effectiveness of this device for this use has not been demonstrated. Adverse reactions observed in clinical studies include hypotension, hypothermia, tachycardia, hyperglycemia, and thrombocytopenia. Additional risks may include blood loss or extracorporeal circuit complications. QUELIMMUNE must be used with citrate anticoagulation.

 

For complete risk information, please see: https://seastarmedical.com/quelimmune 

 

About the SeaStar Medical Selective Cytopheretic Device (SCD) Therapy

 

The SCD therapy is designed as a disease-modifying device that neutralizes over-active immune cells and stops the cytokine storm that yields destructive hyperinflammation and creates a cascade of events that wreak havoc in the patient’s body. The SCD therapy is designed for broad applications in multiple acute and chronic kidney and cardiovascular diseases, representing patients who today have no FDA-approved options for treating their disease.  Unlike pathogen removal and other blood-purification tools, the SCD therapy is integrated with an existing CRRT hemofiltration system to selectively target and transition proinflammatory monocytes to a reparative state and promote activated neutrophils to be less inflammatory. This unique immunomodulation approach may promote long-term organ recovery, eliminate the need for future CRRT, including dialysis, and prevent loss of life.  

 

About NEUTRALIZE-AKI Pivotal Trial

 

The NEUTRALIZE-AKI (NEUTRophil and monocyte deActivation via SeLective Cytopheretic Device – a randomIZEd clinical trial in AKI) pivotal trial is evaluating the safety and efficacy of the SCD therapy in 339 adults with AKI in the ICU receiving CRRT. The trial’s primary endpoint is a composite of 90-day mortality or dialysis dependency of patients treated with the SCD therapy in addition to CRRT as the standard of care, compared with the control group receiving only CRRT standard of care. Secondary endpoints include mortality at 28 days, ICU-free days in the first 28 days, major adverse kidney events at Day 90 and dialysis dependency at one year. The study will also include subgroup analyses to explore the effectiveness of the SCD therapy in AKI patients with sepsis and acute respiratory distress syndrome. 

 

About Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) and Hyperinflammation 

 

AKI is characterized by a sudden and temporary loss of kidney function and can be caused by a variety of conditions such as severe infections or other septic conditions, severe trauma, surgery, and organ failures. AKI can cause destructive hyperinflammation, which is the overproduction or overactivity of inflammatory effector cells and other molecules that can be toxic. Damage resulting from this destructive hyperinflammation in AKI can progress to other organs, such as the heart or liver, and potentially to multi-organ dysfunction or even failure that could result in worse outcomes, including increased risk of death. Even after resolution, these patients may face complications including chronic kidney disease or end-stage renal disease (ESRD) requiring dialysis. Extreme hyperinflammation may also contribute to added healthcare costs, such as prolonged ICU stays and increased reliance on dialysis and mechanical ventilation.

About SeaStar Medical

 

SeaStar Medical is a commercial-stage healthcare company focused on transformational treatments for critically ill patients facing organ failure and potential loss of life. SeaStar Medical’s first commercial product, QUELIMMUNE (SCD-PED), was approved in 2024 by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). It is the only FDA approved product for the ultra-rare condition of life-threatening Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) due to sepsis or a septic condition requiring renal replacement therapy (RRT) in critically ill pediatric patients. SeaStar Medical’s Selective Cytopheretic Device (SCD) therapy has been awarded Breakthrough Device Designation for seven therapeutic indications by the FDA, enabling the potential for a speedier pathway to approval and preferable reimbursement dynamics at commercial launch. The company is currently conducting the NEUTRALIZE-AKI pivotal clinical trial of its SCD therapy in adult patients with AKI requiring continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), a life-threatening condition with no effective treatment options that impacts over 200,000 adults in the U.S. annually.

 

For more information visit www.seastarmedical.com or visit us on LinkedIn or X.
